title: The true friend
hookLine: false friends and true friends, and how to tell them apart
last: TOO HOT, TOO LATE, TOO TIRED.

cards: Moving day. You've asked around: anyone free Saturday? One friend sends ten heart emojis and a long message about how much they wish they could.
One says they'll be there, then asks to borrow your car next week. One goes quiet. And one just shows up at eight with coffee and a dolly, and stays until the last box is in.
The Sigalovada has a name for every one of them.

teach.h: THE TAKER, THE TALKER, THE FLATTERER.
teach.b: First, the Buddha tells Sigala, there are four who look like friends and aren't. The taker gives little and asks a lot, and helps only out of fear or for his own gain.
The talker is all words: generous about the past and the future, but when you need something now, he points to his bad luck.

The flatterer agrees with whatever you do, good or bad, praises you to your face, and runs you down behind your back. And the companion in wasting is your partner for drinking, roaming at night, shows and gambling.
The helper looks after you when you're careless, guards your things, is a refuge when you're afraid, and when there's a job to do, gives you twice what you asked for.

teach.h: THE SAME IN GOOD AND BAD.
teach.b: The one who's the same in good times and bad tells you his secrets, keeps yours, doesn't leave you when things go wrong, and would give his life for you.

teach.h: THE ONE WHO POINTS THE WAY.
teach.b: The one who points the way keeps you from wrong, encourages what's good, tells you what you haven't heard, and points out the way to heaven.

And the one who cares doesn't celebrate your bad luck, is glad at your good luck, stops others when they speak ill of you, and praises those who speak well of you. Every test is something you can watch for.
And there's a mirror in it: the same list tells you what kind of friend to be.

how: Buddhist teachers teach the Sigalovada's eight kinds of friend to young people and families, and the Buddha's wider teaching calls good friendship, kalyanamittata, the whole of the holy life.

o: a teacher whose orders you must obey
a friend, one who stands by you
a business partner who shares profits

games.q: the true friend: tap the pairs.
p: generous about past and future only
praises to your face, runs you down later

s: the flatterer agrees only with your good actions
he approves of whatever you do, good or bad.
the true helper gives twice what you asked for
when there's a job to do.
the one who cares stops others from speaking ill of you
and praises those who speak well of you.

games.q: you need help now. a friend says how much he'd have helped last month, and how he'll help next year, but today he's unlucky. which kind of friend is he?
games.why: the talker: generous about past and future, empty in the present.

practice: Let one true friend come to mind, someone who showed up, and picture the moment: what they did, how it felt. Breathe that gratitude in.
Then ask quietly which of the four true friends you are to someone: the helper, the steady one, the one who points the way, or the one who cares.

wordCard.voice: mitta. In DN 31, four false friends and four true ones: the helper, the steady one, the one who points the way, and the one who cares. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali mitta: friend. a true friend is called suhada, good-hearted.

carryVoice: Your line: the friend in need. The one who shows up at eight. Day five hundred sixty-nine, done.
